I walked through a mountain trail brimming with overgrowth. I parked the car I drove in the town at the foot of the mountain. I avoided the closed-off asphalt path and instead entered through a mountain trail in the forest. It had been a while since I was last here. Three years had passed since I escaped from that underground facility. Those years really did feel like they flew by. I was still working for Natsuki-san. I thought I was going to die from all the learning I had to do. But I was still here, alive, even after undertaking a number of missions where I seriously did come close to dying. There was something I was curious about when I was first acquiring those necessary skills under Natsuki-san’s instruction. It was regarding the old man who raised me. His main job was repairing cart bikes. He took me all over Japan as he traveled. He was also incredibly strong. That’s why I asked Natsuki-san the following..."Why didn’t my old man teach me how to be strong...?"She smiled and replied, "He probably wanted to let you lead a normal life."... Hearing that made me think something else, though. Perhaps my old man and Natsuki-san actually knew each other? I wasn’t able to ask her that, though. I think I was afraid... Afraid of finding out my old man’s true identity. I wanted him to remain inside of my mind as the kind man who raised me. I wanted him to not have any relation to the people involved with "paradise" and whatnot. I ended up finding out the truth from someone else eventually. That someone was another mercenary who had known Natsuki-san for a long time. He was a kind man with a thick beard. If someone had told me he was some random old farmer, I would’ve believed them. He was very friendly to me. He also knew my old man. My old man was a mercenary. It was strange to me how, even in a peaceful country like Japan, mercenaries and hitmen could easily be learned about once you enter "that" side of the world. My old man knew me very well. He was involved in the incident where I met Nemu, was eventually captured, and had my memory erased. He knew what happened to me after that, as well. My old man apparently said that I was a very unfortunate kid. The kind of kid who was involved in not one, but two disasters that most people would likely never experience in their lives. I was just an unlucky, worthless kid once those incidents I was involved in were over. My old man said this after he saw what happened to me in those two incidents."That’s enough. This kid’s experienced enough misfortune for ten people. He doesn’t need to suffer any longer.""So I’m going to take him with me.""He deserves to experience normal happiness. I don’t know if someone like me who only knows battle is the best person to teach him that, but...".................. The old mercenary who told me all these things also said that Natsuki-san was one of my old man’s subordinates at one point. I... Never told Natsuki-san about the things that old mercenary told me. And I stopped complaining after that. Natsuki-san was indeed a strict teacher. She never branded me as a failure, but my progress could hardly be said to have gone well. Eventually, I did acquire the necessary skills to work as a pro and... I did indeed reach the point where I was able to complete missions on my own. That was... my classroom. That was where I reunited with Nemu at the beginning of my second year. Where I had class, talked about trivial stuff with my classmates, ate lunch... And where that death game began. That all happened a mere three years ago, yet it felt like those events were over a decade old.... cos(h) sin(A) = -cos(δ) sin(H). cos(h) cos(A) = cos(ψ) sin(δ) -sin(ψ) cos(δ) cos(H). sin(h) = sin(ψ) sin(δ) +cos(ψ) cos(δ) cos(H). h = altitude. A = azimuth. δ = declination. ψ = latitude. H = hour angle. Zenith was self-explanatory. And finally, those numbers. There were more than enough hints. The puzzle pieces began to come together inside of my head. The final piece was those days I spent with Kanae. The fake Kanae. Back when she was still my precious childhood friend. There was no need for me to download any data. I took out my smartphone. I already had the data I needed ready. I input those characters into my smartphone. I easily obtained the components I needed for that formula. I calculated Kanae’s location right there. The application would calculate the latitude and longitude coordinates from the numbers and formula I had and would then transfer that information to the GPS in my smartphone.
